spatial_claims.claim: AB and CD lie in the same plane P (by definition of parallel lines, D1.23)
E is in plane P (since E is on AB)
F is in plane P (since F is on CD)
G is on segment EF between E and F
E, G, F are collinear (G lies on EF)
H is on AB, distinct from E
F is not on line AB (AB parallel to CD prevents intersection)
Triangle EHF lies in some plane Q (by 11.2)
Segment EH lies in plane Q; by 11.1, entire line AB lies in plane Q
F is in plane Q (vertex of triangle EHF)
EF lies in plane Q (side of triangle EHF)
H, E, F are non-collinear (F not on line AB) and determine plane Q uniquely
Plane P contains H, E, F; since these are non-collinear and determine a unique plane, P = Q

configuration_map: Plane P: defined as the plane containing parallel lines AB and CD (D1.23). Points E (on AB) and F (on CD) are both in P. Point H is on AB, distinct from E, also in P. Triangle EHF has all three vertices in P. Plane Q is defined as the plane of triangle EHF (by 11.2). Since segment EH is in Q, line AB is in Q (by 11.1). Since EF is a side of triangle EHF, EF is in Q. Both P and Q contain the three non-collinear points H, E, F (non-collinear because F is not on line AB). Three non-collinear points determine a unique plane, so P = Q. Therefore EF lies in P, the plane of the parallel lines.
pass_reason: All spatial claims concern plane membership and are mutually consistent. The key argument (P = Q via shared non-collinear points H, E, F) is valid. There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior point arguments, and no contradictory betweenness or ray-ordering claims. The abandoned contradiction attempt in Steps 3-5 introduces no binding claims used in the final proof.
